title: The water in three bottles activity
body: A teacher gives students seven 'water in three bottles' problems. Bottles A, B and C have fixed capacities, and the student must measure out a required quantity. In problems 1 to 5 the answer is always reached by the sequence B - A - 2C: fill B, pour out enough to fill A once, then fill C twice. For example, with A = 21 ml, B = 127 ml and C = 3 ml, 127 - 21 - 3 - 3 = 100 ml. In problem 6 (A = 23, B = 49, C = 3, required 20 ml), the old sequence works, but simply pouring from A into C is quicker. In problem 7 (A = 28, B = 76, C = 3, required 25 ml), only the simple method A - C works. The teacher finds that many students solve problem 6 by the long sequence and then get stuck on problem 7.
